FIVE INDIVIDUAL FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F121 / Quantum-Chemical Simulation of Aroma Electronic Structure at the Limit The proposed physical object is electronic-structure prediction of authenticated botanical odorant molecules, with emphasis on electron correlation, density functional approximation, basis-set incompleteness, spin state, reference geometry, stereochemistry, pseudopotential choice and convergence diagnostics. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. Potentially stronger rival: conformer omission, changed reference geometry or inconsistent electronic reference state rather than an improved Hamiltonian approximation. Hard stop: missing independent energy reference, uncontrolled charge or spin, nonconvergent SCF or undisclosed multi-reference character. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F121, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F122 / Conformational Energy Landscapes of Botanical Terpenes at the Limit The proposed physical object is ranking of torsional conformers in complex botanical terpene stereoisomers, with emphasis on torsional potential energy, conformer search coverage, Boltzmann populations, thermal barriers, stereo- and enantiomer assignment, correlated energy errors and duplicated minima. Primary decision: Conformer rank agreement (Kendall tau) [ratio]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs authenticated cis/trans and enantiomeric terpene structures, archived conformer search seeds and blinded reference-energy sets. Compare to exhaustive classical conformer search followed by the same high-level electronic reference and preregistered rank agreement. An independent observer must evaluate independent deduplicated conformer geometries, high-level relative energies and tie-aware Kendall tau calculated on withheld structures. Blinded adversarial intervention: hidden mirror-image stereoisomer and duplicate-conformer injection before blinded re-ranking. Potentially stronger rival: undersampled conformers, duplicate conformer labels or biased tie treatment falsely improving agreement. Hard stop: unresolved stereoisomer identity, insufficient conformer coverage, unstable ranking under resampling or ill-defined Kendall tau denominator. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F122, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F123 / Quantum-Chemical Models of Aroma–Olfactory-Receptor Binding at the Limit The proposed physical object is molecular interaction energy of odorant ligands and uncertain receptor-pocket models, with emphasis on ligand protonation, flexible receptor pocket geometry, solvent dielectric screening, dispersion interactions, desolvation, entropy, charge assignment and uncertain structural identity. Primary decision: Receptor-binding energy prediction MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs documented synthetic ligand-pocket cluster coordinates, archived reference structures and separately labelled hypothetical receptor conformations. Compare to matched classical force-field plus high-level cluster quantum chemistry with explicit solvation controls and an independent binding reference if available. An independent observer must evaluate holdout geometry and binding-energy benchmark with independent structural annotation and environmental assumptions. Blinded adversarial intervention: blind receptor-pocket rotamer and protonation swap with a decoy ligand of identical size. Potentially stronger rival: docking pose selection or solvent/protonation mismatch yielding attractive computed energies without genuine binding. Hard stop: undefined receptor structure or protonation, no legitimate reference binding energy, uncorrected double-counting or model interpreting binding as sensory effect. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F123, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F124 / Quantum Chemistry of Essential-Oil Oxidation Pathways at the Limit The proposed physical object is oxidative transition states and competing reaction pathways for terpene constituents, with emphasis on radical initiation, oxygen addition, hydrogen transfer, conformer-dependent transition states, spin-state crossings, intrinsic reaction coordinates, zero-point corrections and branching competing channels. Primary decision: Oxidation transition-state energy error [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally defined terpene oxidation reactants, radicals and transition-state coordinate sets; no synthesized reactive intermediates. Compare to same-stationary-point reference transition-state energies using established electronic-structure methods with vibrational and IRC verification. An independent observer must evaluate independent harmonic frequency/IRC files, matched reaction states, oxygen accounting and high-level reference barrier energies. Blinded adversarial intervention: withheld spin-state and competing oxygen-addition channel with randomized path labels. Potentially stronger rival: wrong saddle order, missing radical branch, inconsistent spin reference or mismatched zero-point energy. Hard stop: transition structure without one valid imaginary mode and connected IRC, unaccounted oxygen stoichiometry or severe reference-state mismatch. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F124, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F125 / Photochemical Degradation of Aroma Molecules at the Limit The proposed physical object is light-driven transformation rates, absorption cross sections and competing oxygen pathways, with emphasis on wavelength-dependent photon absorption, excited-state quantum yield, oxygen-quenching, radical photoproduct branches, nonradiative loss and dark-reaction baselines. Primary decision: Photochemical degradation rate coefficient [h^-1]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs traceable simulated terpene chromophores, documented absorption spectra and synthetic photon flux distributions with reference lamp metadata. Compare to classical spectral photokinetic model with measured lamp spectrum, blanks and matched dark control; high-level photochemical calculations for candidate cross-sections. An independent observer must evaluate independent actinometry, spectrum-resolved photolysis and chemical parent/product inventory from a future experiment. Blinded adversarial intervention: concealed wavelength filter swap, oxygen-clamp reversal and dark-control code exchange. Potentially stronger rival: spectral lamp drift, oxygen ingress or parent-molecule assay loss masquerading as photolytic degradation. Hard stop: unmeasured lamp spectrum, missing parent-plus-photoproduct balance, nonidentified reaction rate or unstable photon-dose calibration. Units: E_calc and E_ref in Hartree; 2625.4996 kJ/mol per Hartree; Delta_E kJ/mol. 3D: A reference-residual valley across basis size and conformer count. F121 / Absolute electronic-energy error: MAE = sum(abs(E_i-E_ref,i))/N. Units: All energies kJ/mol; N distinct held-out molecules; MAE kJ/mol. 3D: An error basin whose apparently low corner may omit difficult structures. F121 / Variational state energy: E_var = <psi|H|psi>/<psi|psi>. Units: Numerator energy in Hartree and denominator dimensionless; E_var Hartree. 3D: A variational saddle reflects ansatz expressivity, not quantum advantage. F121 / Basis-set extrapolation: E(X) = E_inf + A*X^(-3). Units: E and A Hartree; cardinal X dimensionless; single-reference asymptotic assumption. 3D: A convergence ridge flattening as X rises. F121 / Molecular energy error uncertainty: u_diff = sqrt(u_calc^2+u_ref^2-2*cov). Units: Both uncertainties Hartree; covariance Hartree^2; u_diff Hartree. 3D: An uncertainty contour may hide correlated reference errors. F121 / Energy improvement per compute cost: G = (MAE_ref-MAE_new)/Cost. Units: Numerator kJ/mol; cost CPU-hour/molecule; G kJ*mol^-1/(CPU-hour/molecule). 3D: The gain-cost ridge may reverse under a full compute budget. F122 / Periodic torsion potential: V(phi)=V0+sum[V_n*(1+cos(n*phi-delta_n))/2]. Units: V0,Vn kJ/mol; phi and phase in radians inside cosine; V kJ/mol. 3D: Periodic torsional ridges identify alternate basins. F122 / Boltzmann conformer probability: p_i=exp(-DeltaE_i/(R*T))/Z. Units: DeltaE kJ/mol; R=0.008314 kJ/(mol*K); T K; Z dimensionless. 3D: Temperature-dependent basin population envelope. F122 / Tie-corrected Kendall agreement: tau_b=(C-D)/sqrt((C+D+Tx)*(C+D+Ty)). Units: C,D,Tx,Ty counts; tau dimensionless in [-1,1]. 3D: Rank-agreement saddle differs from minimum-energy error surface. F122 / Conformer energy root mean square: RMSE=sqrt(sum((Ei-Erefi)^2)/N). Units: E and reference in kJ/mol; result kJ/mol. 3D: An RMSE crest detects catastrophic outliers hidden by rank scores. F122 / Relative partition free energy: F=-R*T*ln(sum_i exp(-DeltaEi/(R*T))). Units: R kJ/(mol*K); T K; F kJ/mol relative to stated energy zero. 3D: A population valley varies with conformer entropy. F122 / Conformer effective sample number: Neff=1/sum_i(p_i^2). Units: p_i dimensionless and normalized; Neff effective count. 3D: Sparse-count plateau indicates a misleading landscape. F123 / Cluster binding energy difference: DeltaE_bind=E_complex-E_receptor-E_ligand. Units: All E in kJ/mol and same electronic reference, charge and basis; DeltaE kJ/mol. 3D: A binding-energy well sensitive to solvent and pose. F123 / Pocket interaction energy error: MAE_bind=sum(abs(Gpred-Gref))/N. Units: All G kJ/mol in the same thermodynamic reference convention. 3D: A hidden pose change can create a false error minimum. F123 / Screened electrostatic interaction: E_C=(NA/(1000*4*pi*eps0*epsr))*sum(qi*qj/rij). Units: qi C, r m, eps0 F/m, NA mol^-1; result kJ/mol. 3D: A dielectric dependent Coulomb valley. F123 / Conformational ensemble binding free energy: DeltaG_eff=-R*T*ln(sum_i p_i*exp(-DeltaG_i/(R*T))). Units: R kJ/(mol*K), T K, G kJ/mol; p_i normalized. 3D: A multi-pocket basin changes under ensemble reweighting. F123 / Binding entropy correction: DeltaG=DeltaH-T*DeltaS. Units: DeltaH kJ/mol; DeltaS kJ/(mol*K); T K; DeltaG kJ/mol. 3D: Entropy term produces a temperature-dependent saddle. F123 / Binding prediction normalized error: z=(G_pred-G_ref)/u_G. Units: G and uncertainty u_G kJ/mol; z dimensionless. 3D: A standardized residual frontier diagnoses false confidence. F124 / Oxidation activation barrier: DeltaE_dagger=E_TS-E_reactants. Units: E_TS and E_reactants kJ/mol with same charge/spin and ZPE convention. 3D: A reaction coordinate saddle must be independently verified. F124 / Transition barrier prediction error: epsilon_TS=DeltaE_dagger,pred-DeltaE_dagger,ref. Units: Both barriers kJ/mol in matching reference convention; error kJ/mol. 3D: A basis-dependent error valley can hide missing reaction channels. F124 / Eyring transition state rate: k=(kB*T/h)*exp(-DeltaG_dagger/(R*T)). Units: kB*T/h s^-1; DeltaG_dagger and RT J/mol; k s^-1. 3D: Rate curvature amplifies modest barrier differences. F124 / Activation free-energy identity: DeltaG_dagger=DeltaH_dagger-T*DeltaS_dagger. Units: DeltaH J/mol; DeltaS J/(mol*K); T K; result J/mol. 3D: Entropy-driven crossing shows why electronic barrier is not Gibbs barrier. F124 / Reaction branching fraction: f_i=k_i/sum_j(k_j). Units: All competing rate constants in same time unit; f dimensionless. 3D: Competing channels make ridges instead of a single preferred path. F124 / Vibrational saddle requirement: N_imag(TS)=1. Units: Count of imaginary harmonic frequencies; dimensionless integer. 3D: A discrete topology gate, not a smooth empirical surface. F125 / Apparent first-order photolysis rate: k_app=-d[ln(C/C0)]/dt. Units: C and C0 same units; t h; k_app h^-1, only within first-order regime. 3D: Decay-rate ridge must match independent parent/product inventory. F125 / Photon-flux photolysis kernel: k_photo=3600*integral(phi(lam)*sigma(lam)*F(lam)dlam). Units: Quantum yield phi dimensionless; sigma m2; spectral photon flux integrated photons/(m2*s); k h^-1. 3D: Action-spectrum crest follows wavelength-resolved absorption. F125 / Beer-Lambert optical absorbance: A=epsilon*c*l. Units: epsilon L/(mol*cm), c mol/L, l cm; absorbance dimensionless. 3D: Absorbance saturation ridge violates linear small-signal expectation. F125 / Molecular photolysis quantum yield: phi=N_reacted/N_absorbed. Units: Photon and reacted molecule counts; phi dimensionless in simple one-photon pathway. 3D: Yield valley tests competing relaxation channels. F125 / Integrated photon fluence: H_photon=integral(F_photon(t) dt). Units: F photons/(m2*s); dt s; fluence photons/m2. 3D: Fluence contours expose different intensity-time schedules. F125 / Photo-dark competing reaction rates: k_total=k_photo+k_dark+k_oxygen. Units: All k in h^-1 for same parent species and valid first-order approximation. 3D: Oxygen-pressure saddle distinguishes independent reaction paths. The sixth preserves failed input decks and a binding stopping rule. EIGHTY-TWO PROGRESSIVE CHAPTERS / THE SIX-PASSAGE SCIENTIFIC METHOD Every chapter begins with a different molecular uncertainty and travels through six progressively stronger gates of evidence. The first passage defines chemical identity and valid reference state. The second states a dimensional mechanism and coordinates on which it could be false. The third freezes independent benchmarks and uncertainty. The fourth injects an unseen competitor. The fifth hands the protocol to an uncoached external quantum-chemistry group. The sixth preserves failed input decks and a binding stopping rule. Every one of the 492 passages contains Mechanism, Measurement and Refutation; the three roles are scientifically different and never turn a model image into a measurement. The full notebook retains the individual chapter arguments, including negative conditions and resource accounting.
